briefings.title: Trade Wars, Fighting Corruption and Rethinking Globalization | Leaders with Francine Lacqua
briefings.tldr: Global trade is facing unprecedented disruption and fragmentation reminiscent of the 1930s, driven by geopolitical tensions, shifting subsidies, and protectionism.

briefings.title: 2026 Annual Wenger Lecture with Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
briefings.channel: AUWCL International and Comparative Legal Studies
briefings.tldr: The global trading system is at a critical "turning point" where the World Trade Organization (WTO) must transition from a state of over-dependence and unilateralism toward "reglobalization"—a process of diversifying supply chains to include marginalized regions while reforming foundational multilateral rules to ensure long-term peace and stability.

briefings.title: Can the WTO Survive a New World Order?–Conversation w/ Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala | The Futures Summit
briefings.tldr: While the global trading system faces significant geopolitical disruptions and supply chain "overdependencies," it remains remarkably resilient; however, the WTO must reform its consensus-based decision-making to better integrate digital trade, green initiatives, and South-South cooperation to move from mere adaptability to long-term robustness.

briefings.title: Global Trade Outlook 2026: press conference
briefings.tldr: Global trade growth is projected to slow significantly from a surprisingly strong 4.6% in 2025 to a modest 1.9% in 2026, as the temporary boosts from AI investment and "front-loading" of imports dissipate amid rising geopolitical risks in the Middle East.

briefings.title: Transparency, Trade and Fighting Corruption Across the Globe - Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
briefings.tldr: Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Director-General of the WTO, asserts that institutional transparency and the strategic use of technology are the most effective deterrents to global corruption, emphasizing that the fight against fraud requires both strong systemic frameworks and unwavering personal integrity.
